correctness.rationale: For arbitrary strictly positive local damping and common-noise amplitudes, the symmetric drift matrix is positive definite and the Lyapunov equation uniquely defines the stationary covariance. The displayed determinant factorization is independently symbolically verified; positivity of component variances and covariance makes its unique zero exactly the Pearson-correlation-one condition. The strong-coupling limit is established by symmetric/antisymmetric modes. For parameters (3,1,1,2), the squared-correlation derivative factors into (3m-4) times a cubic with one positive root beyond 4/3 by Descartes and signs; therefore it has exactly one maximum then one minimum. At noise correlation 99/100 the covariance is positive definite and the derivative quartic has two positive zeros by Descartes and two disjoint sign reversals, proving the robust two-extremum claim. The supplied verify.py reconstructs these results algebraically and compares 20 separately solved covariance systems. Finite checks are secondary, not a proof of universality. No general uniqueness or nonlinear claim is made.

originality.rationale: The nearest full-text sources on spatial synchrony are Kendall et al. (2000), who impose homogeneous discrete-time dynamics and equal forcing magnitudes, and Liebhold et al. (2006), who study heterogeneous discrete-time second-order dynamics and simulated correlations rather than this exact covariance tuning. Neither inspected source states or implies the exact continuous-time unique positive perfect-synchrony formula plus a robust two-turning-point Pearson example under stated assumptions. The general Lyapunov/controllability Gramian rank criterion is prior knowledge and is not claimed as original. Broader Gaussian covariance theorems may imply the specialization; incomplete examination of Ripa (2000) and Ly/Ermentrout (2010) leaves explicit historical-priority risk, so this is a provisional self-review priority assessment.
residual_risks: The general rank-one Gramian criterion is prior mathematical knowledge; unknown broader applied results might explicitly spell out the proposed parameter tuning and reverse correlation response.
The original 2000 Ripa source and 2010 coupled-noise full article were not accessible in full, leaving bounded unresolved implication risk.
Ecological relevance is an ideal stationary linearization; no nonlinear population, immigration, or persistence theorem is claimed.

value.rationale: The classical Moran effect and dispersal-synchrony problem motivate whether migration improves coherence when local relaxation and environmental sensitivity differ. The exact positive perfect-synchrony coupling, subsequent desynchronization, large-migration return to coherence, and persistence of two extrema under imperfect common forcing establish a structural phase of the natural correlation observable. The explicit global algebraic two-turning-point classification and sharp input-eigenvector threshold make this more than a routine covariance calculation or tiny numerical effect; the ecologically interpretable parameter rule is not implied by the homogeneous monotonic case. The ideal linear stationary scope is explicit.
